author: JDMACKA

title: I like this, but some problems
body: If you buy a 'Habitminder ' app you want to build habits. The developers don't seem to have thought about timings. I keep changing my habit list as I'm working out slowly what my real priorities are (!) but not having reminders arrive at specific times and having them all arrive first thing in the morning has a very overwhelming, demotivating effect. I'm going back to my simple list in iPhone 'Notes'. Which is a shame as these guys have already taken my money. It's a good idea but needs some work to get it to a workable concept. Also, it doesn't seem flexible. Say you did 'stretching' (I work either standing at an easel or sitting at a desk a lot) - perhaps you did it already, but there's a timer which doesn't allow you to tick that task. You either do it twice or delete the habit. It's just kind of nonsensical to me, and wastes my time. I also think the design is a bit dark and demonic and could be a bit perkier, without being tonally so patronising. I want to try again but this app just isn't helping and there's no online support apparent.

author: ekaterina.d

title: Amazing
body:
I have started using this app after trying many different ones. The interface is great, and works perfectly. 
The way it links into Apple Health (optionally) is a unique touch of genius. For example, if I create a habit to use the Breathe app on my Apple Watch for say, 15 minutes a day. As I use it, I can see the minutes in HabitMinder. When I reach my 15 minute goal, it automatically marks that as complete. 
I emailed support with a suggestion and they responded very quickly. 
Offers a paid subscription, but also an option for a one time lifetime payment. I like this because subscriptions are a real pain (in my opinion). 
Then you can see stats and history so it's easy to see where you can improve.
